seoTitle: How to Access the Google Workspace Admin Console
metaDescription: Sign in to admin.google.com with the right Google account, confirm you have admin permissions, and find your way around the Admin console dashboard.
intro: The most common reason people can't reach the Google Workspace Admin Console isn't a broken link or a bug — it's being signed into the wrong Google account. Google lets you stay logged into several accounts at once, and only the one with admin rights on your Workspace domain will actually open the console. This guide walks through picking the right account from the switcher, confirming you've landed in the real Admin console rather than a regular Gmail view, and finding where the important settings actually live in the sidebar.

steps.heading: Check which Google account you're signed in as
steps.body: Before anything else, click your profile circle in the top-right corner of any Google page. This opens the account switcher showing "Google Account" details for whichever profile is active — in this case "PMN Online" with the address admin@pmntechfix.nl. If you manage multiple Workspace domains or also use a personal Gmail account, this is the step people skip, and it's the reason admin.google.com sometimes seems to "not work" — it's not broken, you're just signed in as the wrong person.

image.caption: The Google account switcher panel, showing the currently active profile's name and email address.

steps.heading: Pick the admin account if you have several
steps.body: If more than one Google account is signed in on your device, the switcher lists them all — in this example, one row for "PMN Online" at proapptechs.com@gmail.com, another "PMN Online" at admin@pmntechfix.nl, and a third labeled "Admin YT PMN" at a different domain entirely. Only the account tied to your Workspace domain as an admin will open the Admin console properly, so select that specific one rather than whichever account happens to be active by default.

image.caption: A list of signed-in Google accounts, with the Workspace admin account (admin@pmntechfix.nl) highlighted among several others.

steps.heading: Go to admin.google.com
steps.body: With the correct account active, navigate directly to admin.google.com rather than trying to find the Admin console through Gmail's app switcher — it's a separate application with its own address, not a tab inside Gmail. If the account you're using has admin rights, this takes you straight to the Admin console Home dashboard rather than an access-denied page.

steps.heading: Get oriented in the sidebar
steps.body: The Admin console's left sidebar is where every setting lives, organized into sections: Directory, Devices, Apps, Generative AI, Security, Data, Reporting, Billing, and Account. The Account section itself expands into Account settings, Admin roles, Domains, Rules, and Storage — so if you're looking for domain-related settings specifically, that's where they are, not under Apps or Directory where it's easy to assume they'd sit.

image.caption: The Admin console sidebar expanded to the Account section, with Account settings, Admin roles, and Domains listed underneath.

steps.heading: Confirm your permission level
steps.body: If you're signed into the right account but sections of the sidebar look grayed out or missing entirely, your account likely has a limited admin role rather than full Super Admin access. Check under Account > Admin roles to see what's actually assigned to you, or ask whoever manages your organization's Workspace account to confirm your role — some settings, particularly Security and Billing, are often restricted to Super Admins specifically.

steps.heading: Troubleshoot if you still can't get in
steps.body: If admin.google.com won't load correctly even with the right account selected, try a different browser or an incognito/private window to rule out a cached session or extension interference. If login itself fails, double-check the exact email address for typos, since Workspace accounts on custom domains are easy to mistype compared to a standard @gmail.com address. If no admin account is available to you at all, that requires going through Google's account recovery process rather than anything fixable from the login screen.

faq.question: Why can't I access the Admin Console even though I'm logged into Google?
faq.answer: You're likely signed into the wrong account. Click your profile circle to open the account switcher and select the specific account that has admin rights on your Workspace domain.

faq.question: How do I find out if I'm a Super Admin?
faq.answer: In the Admin console, go to Account > Admin roles to see your assigned permission level, or check with your organization's IT team if you don't have console access at all.

faq.question: What should I do if I've lost admin access entirely?
faq.answer: If no other admin exists in your organization, you may need to go through Google's account recovery process to regain administrative rights.

faq.question: Can I access the Admin Console from any device?
faq.answer: Yes, the Admin Console works on both desktop and mobile browsers, though desktop is generally easier for more complex settings like Domains and Security.

faq.question: Why does admin.google.com show a different view than I expect?
faq.answer: It's often because multiple Google accounts are signed in on the same device. Check the account switcher in the top-right corner and confirm you've selected the correct Workspace admin account before troubleshooting further.
